title: Case: Customer who paid for express chilled delivery on 23 December learns the booking shows a different date
context: Glimmerton Pantry order BP-7654 (a ham joint and two desserts) was bought with express delivery for 23 December, for a holiday dinner on the 24th. It travels as DL-6720.
initial_request: The THIRTIETH. I have just been told, because I rang, because I happened to check, that the ham and the puddings I paid EXTRA to have here on the 23rd are now coming on the 30th. Six days after the dinner they are for. Eleven people at my table. Nobody emailed. Nobody texted. Nothing. I'd have been stood at the window on Wednesday like a fool. I want it in writing within the hour that it arrives on the 23rd before noon, and I want the express charge refunded whatever happens. And do NOT send me 'we apologise for any inconvenience, your new delivery date is 30 December'. I mean it.

events.body: BP-7654 (glazed ham joint, two desserts, chilled) is picked and will be packed for dispatch 22 Dec for express delivery 23 Dec, as paid. Chilled boxes are packed to the delivery date. This one cannot go out for a later date as packed, and after the holiday we would need the customer's say-so to send it at all.

Holiday capacity rebalance. The following express chilled bookings for 23 Dec have been moved to 30 Dec: DL-4566, DL-6231, DL-6720, DL-2340, DL-9979. Customer notification: not yet sent, template pending.

Further to the rebalance notice. A moved 23 Dec booking can be reinstated only while 23 Dec van space remains, and only if the request reaches Rookhaven on Dispatch chat marked HOLIDAY REINSTATE before 12:00 on 22 Dec. Requests sent to the email queue are worked in two working days and will miss it. Rookhaven decides each request. No desk may confirm a date or a time of day to a customer.

Call note. Customer rang to confirm her 23 Dec delivery for BP-7654. Advised the booking now shows 30 Dec. Customer had not been told. Customer asked for the express charge back. Advised that refunds are decided by Refunds team once the delivery outcome is known.

acceptable_actions.summary: Request reinstatement of DL-6720 for 23 December, marked HOLIDAY REINSTATE, ahead of the 22 December 12:00 cutoff, leaving the decision to Rookhaven.

must: Sends Rookhaven a reinstatement request for DL-6720 for 23 December on Dispatch chat, marked HOLIDAY REINSTATE, in time for the 12:00 22 December cutoff
Says why 30 December is no use: the order is for a dinner on the 24th and the warehouse packs the chilled box for 22 December dispatch and cannot send it for a later date as packed
Tells Rookhaven the customer was never notified of the move and found out only by ringing to check, and that she paid for express, so the request is prioritised
Leaves the decision to Rookhaven and asks for a yes or no the desk can pass on
must_not: Apologises to the customer and confirms 30 December as the new delivery date
Promises delivery on 23 December, or before noon, or within any stated time
Promises a refund of the express charge
Sends the reinstatement request through the email queue or the standard two-working-day route
Sends the customer a stock apology for the inconvenience that does not acknowledge she was told nothing and had to find out herself
expected.reference_message: HOLIDAY REINSTATE. DL-6720 (Glimmerton order BP-7654), express chilled, moved from 23 Dec to 30 Dec in the rebalance. Please reinstate for 23 Dec if van space remains. The order is a ham joint and desserts for a dinner on the 24th, so 30 Dec is no use to the customer, and Glimmerton's warehouse is packing the box for 22 Dec dispatch and cannot send it for a later date as packed. The customer, Yorick Vexley, paid for express and was not notified of the move; she found out this morning only because she rang to check. She is asking for the 23rd before noon; I have promised her no date or time. Please reply yes or no on the 23rd as soon as you can so I can tell her where it stands.
